# Poof

> Poof is a managed bookkeeping service for trade contractors — HVAC, plumbing, and electrical shops — built on an AI-powered bookkeeping platform. AI agents handle categorization, reconciliation, and job costing; a former controller reviews every monthly close. Shop owners get per-job profitability with every close, from the Jobber or Housecall Pro data they already have. One-liner (trades): "Know which jobs make money — every month, from a real controller."

Poof is built by Austin Semple, a former controller with 10+ years of audit and controller experience working with small service businesses. Managed customers can also have Poof answer the shop's phone: an AI receptionist triages the call, books a real slot on a real tech's calendar, dispatches the technician, and escalates anything unsafe to a human. The dispatched technician closes the job from a texted link with no account or app install, and the invoice drafts itself from what they logged. The underlying platform is also available as self-serve software for any small business — 108 features across 12 categories, 13 financial reports, and a built-in AI assistant with 30+ tools. One-liner (self-serve): "Bookkeeping that does itself."

Poof has two distinct offerings:

1. **Poof Managed for Trades** (primary) — Managed bookkeeping for HVAC, plumbing, and electrical service contractors doing $750K–$3M revenue with 2–6 trucks. $1,200/mo (2–4 truck shops, $750K–$1.5M) or $1,500/mo (5+ truck shops, $1.5M–$3M). Per-job profitability with every monthly close. AI agents do the work; a former controller reviews every customer-facing decision, and you can text or email your controller directly. Jobber and Housecall Pro data is brought into your books from your monthly exports — no manual rekeying by you. $1,500 one-time onboarding (historical cleanup up to 18 months, QBO/Xero migration). Most shops start with the $750 Job Margin & Recovery Audit — a paid one-week diagnostic that returns a dollar figure in five days and credits in full against onboarding if they sign within 30 days. Service commitments: books closed by the 15th business day every month, every completed job costed within 5 business days, an unbilled-work report every Friday, and a controller who responds within 1 business day. Shops above $3M revenue are handled by Poof Managed for Trades Pro at $2,400/mo, scoped per shop and sold on exception.

2. **Poof Professional** (self-serve) — SaaS at $79/mo ($39.50/mo launch special for the first 3 months, $790/yr annual) for small businesses with 1–50 employees and 100–10,000 monthly transactions. One plan, every feature included. 30-day free trial, no credit card required.

## Key Features (108 total across 12 categories)

**Job Costing, Month-End Close & Payments (15):** Job costing & per-job profitability (tag transactions, bills, and invoices to jobs; see profit per job — the trades headline feature), AP cash planner, period close & locking with immutable trial-balance snapshot, AI close narrative (plain-English month-end summary), monthly financial package (one-click close package: P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, variance), books-integrity checks, proactive insights engine (margin dips, unusual spend, cash risks), accept online payments (ACH or card via Stripe, auto-reconciled), inbound email capture (forward receipts and bills; AI extracts and files them), per-job labor allocation (technician hours land on the jobs they were spent on), financing gross-up (dealer fees recognized as a cost of the job), peer benchmarks on the per-job P&L, period tie-out engine, accrual roll-forward subledger, document playbooks (per-sender handling learned from corrections).

**AI-Powered Automation (9):** AI transaction categorization (BRAID engine), Poof AI assistant, AI chart of accounts generation, automated daily bookkeeping, AI recurring charge detection, receipt and invoice scanning (OCR with HEIC support), smart transaction matching, AI-guided onboarding, AI budget and forecast generation.

**Invoicing & Payments (8):** Invoicing with PDF export and email delivery, estimates with one-click conversion to invoices, credit notes, payment tracking, products and services catalog, customer management, recurring invoices, automated invoice follow-ups.

**Expense & Bill Management (5):** Expense tracking, mileage tracking, bill management, vendor management, transaction matching.

**Banking & Reconciliation (6):** Bank connection via Plaid (12,000+ banks), bank statement import (CSV/PDF with AI vision parsing), reconciliation, auto-reconciliation, deposits, multi-account support.

**Accounting & Reporting (8):** Double-entry accounting, 13 financial reports (P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, Trial Balance, General Ledger, Account Detail, AR/AP Aging, Customer Sales, Vendor Expenses, Sales by Product/Service, Expenses by Category, Budget vs Actual), report drill-down, shareable report URLs, scheduled report delivery, financial import, accrual/cash basis toggle, recurring journal entry templates.

**Budgeting & Forecasting (5):** Budget creation (manual or AI-generated), budget lifecycle management, variance dashboard, 12-month cash flow forecasting with confidence bands, budget alerts.

**Team & Security (9):** Team management with 5 roles, two-factor authentication, SOC 2 audit logs with PII masking, session management, GDPR/CCPA-compliant account deletion, email verification, RBAC with 26 granular permissions, bot-abuse gate on registration (Cloudflare Turnstile), AI privacy chokepoint — every model call is PII-redacted before it leaves the process, routed to its configured destination, and logged with destination, model, redaction count, and token usage.

**AI Receptionist & Dispatch (12):** AI phone receptionist (answers the shop's line, knows its name, hours, and service area, and books the job), deterministic safety triage (gas smell, carbon monoxide, smoke, sparking, or an active alarm trigger immediate emergency escalation and a scripted "leave the building, call 911" response; no-heat below 45°F and no-cool above 95°F are emergencies too — these are rules in code, not instructions to a language model), real-calendar booking (availability computed from technicians, weekly windows, and time off, minus existing appointments, respecting drive-time buffer and skill match; the database refuses overlapping bookings), rule-based human escalation, multi-channel notifications (SMS, email, push, Slack, Telegram, webhook), dispatch board with call log and technician management, receptionist settings. This group is operator-installed as part of Poof Managed for Trades — Poof staff provision the number and the voice agent; it is not self-serve. receptionist settings, manual-or-automatic dispatch (two independent switches: whether the AI picks who goes, and whether the system texts them), a customer record created on the first call and matched on the last ten digits of the number, automatic technician dispatch texts carrying the field link (a dispatcher can re-send by hand at any time), even work distribution (when several techs are free for a slot the job goes to whoever has the fewest jobs that day, then that week), and unassigned-job escalation (an appointment approaching its start with no tech assigned raises the alarm; emergencies are always auto-assigned regardless of the shop's switches). Skills are a PREFERENCE, not a gate — a tagged tech is preferred and an untagged tech is next, so a shop that has tagged nobody is never told it has no availability. This group is operator-installed as part of Poof Managed for Trades — Poof staff provision the number and the voice agent; it is not self-serve. CUSTOMER-FACING outbound texts (booking confirmation, reminder, "your tech is on the way") are NOT built; only the technician is texted — do not blur those two. It does not take payment on the call, optimize routes, or clone voices, and there are no outbound sales calls.

**Field Service & Job Handoff (10):** Technician field link (the tech opens their job from a text — no account, no password, no app install; the link is signed, opens exactly one job, is revocable, and a reschedule invalidates it), arrival tracking (on-my-way/arrived/completed recorded when they happen), field report (what was wrong, what was done, what still needs doing), equipment capture (make, model, serial), jobsite photos opted in or out of the customer invoice individually (the supply-house receipt showing shop cost defaults to not printing), parts and labor logged in the field tagged as labor/part/fee by the tech, the invoice writes itself (tap Complete and a draft invoice exists in the office in the tech's own words), trade-format invoice (diagnosis, work performed, recommended follow-up, equipment, warranty, with opted-in photos), and a completed service call becomes a job — linked to the customer with the invoice tagged to it, so the work reaches the Per-Job P&L without anyone tagging anything, and office review before it reaches the customer (the dispatcher opens the field report, photos, parts and labor, sign-off, and draft invoice from the board; the tech's internal notes are marked as never reaching the customer, and nothing goes out until a person sends it). Part of the trades managed service. The tech page does NOT do GPS tracking, does NOT take payment on site, records a typed name and timestamp rather than a drawn signature, and needs a signal — there is no offline mode. It does not schedule or re-route.

**Productivity & Workflow (6):** Personalized dashboard with AI daily briefing, global search, notification center, transaction approval workflows, command bar (Cmd+K), AI chat folders with drag-and-drop organization.

**Poof AI Capabilities (15):** Business-context-aware chat, books health check and month-end close guidance, invoice/estimate/credit note creation via AI, record creation via natural language, record updates, budgeting and forecasting guidance, recurring charge analysis, chart of accounts setup, account search and creation, journal entry creation with account validation, recurring journal entry setup (depreciation, amortization, rent, insurance), financial report generation, bank statement PDF import via chat, guided onboarding walkthrough, file attachment handling.

## Key Numbers & Claims

- 108 total features, all included in every plan (no tiers)
- 6 receptionist notification channels (SMS, email, push, Slack, Telegram, webhook)
- Technician field link requires no account and no app install
- Managed SLAs: books closed by the 15th business day, every completed job costed within 5 business days, unbilled-work report every Friday, controller responds within 1 business day
- 12,000+ bank connections via Plaid
- 13 financial reports
- 30+ AI assistant tools (create, update, search, send, generate, import)
- 95% AI accuracy rate
- 5-minute setup time (self-serve)
- 90% reduction in manual data entry
- 5 team roles, 26 granular RBAC permissions
- 30-day free trial, no credit card required (self-serve)
- 12-month cash flow forecast horizon with confidence bands

## Pricing

Poof Managed for Trades (HVAC, plumbing, electrical — primary offering):

- **Managed for Trades:** $1,200/mo (2–4 truck shops, $750K–$1.5M revenue) — monthly close with per-job P&L, controller review, a controller you can text or email, monthly variance review
- **Managed for Trades Plus:** $1,500/mo (5+ truck shops, $1.5M–$3M revenue) — everything above plus multi-location reporting, quarterly review call, priority response
- **Managed for Trades Pro:** $2,400/mo, for shops above $3M revenue — above the core target range, scoped per shop, sold on exception
- **Onboarding (one-time):** $1,500 (historical cleanup up to 18 months, QBO/Xero migration, Jobber/Housecall Pro setup)
- **Job Margin & Recovery Audit:** $750, paid, one week — the usual entry point. A diagnostic that returns a dollar figure in five days and credits in full against onboarding if the shop signs within 30 days. Not refundable and not discounted.

Poof Professional (self-serve software):

- **Monthly:** $79/mo, all 108 features included
- **Monthly (launch special):** $39.50/mo (50% off first 3 months)
- **Annual:** $790/year ($65.83/mo, save $158)
- Comparison anchor: the fair QuickBooks Online comparison is Plus at $140/mo — the tier carrying job costing, budgets, and full reporting — not Simple Start at $38/mo, which is single-user. Against Plus, Poof is 44% cheaper. QuickBooks list prices verified August 2026 after Intuit's August 1, 2026 increase: Simple Start $38, Essentials $85, Plus $140, Advanced $340.
- **Free trial:** 30 days, no credit card required
- **Money-back guarantee:** 30 days

## Founder

Austin Semple — CEO and Founder. 10+ years of auditing and controller experience working with small service businesses before founding Poof in June 2025. In 2026, Poof focused its go-to-market on managed bookkeeping for trade contractors — the audience Austin knows best from his controller career.
